Bridgeplain City has been added to the census. It has preserved schools from the old world and excels at organizing and teaching knowledge, but basic medicine requires more staff. First, have the locals establish a public station. Then use “Locally Funded” to build the Lakeside–Bridgeplain School Road. Both ends must provide construction materials and assign 20 workers each for 300 seconds. Once open, the one-way trip takes 240 seconds.

Two Hubin census takers followed the old school road along the north shore to Qiaoyuan. The existing cities have established generational succession and cross-city recruitment. Newly found settlements must likewise support themselves and build their own public stations and connecting roads.

Qiaoyuan residents registered in the census: {变量1}, verified and separated out from the register of those lost to contact in the Northern Lands. Local school buildings, books, and knowledge output remain under local control. Building a public station and opening the Hubin–Qiaoyuan school road both require allocated materials and construction work.
Qiaoyuan already has a public station project

Qiaoyuan draws on its own stocks to build a public station, with 20 local residents beginning work. The schools still prioritize local children. Supplies for other settlements must wait until the road is open.
